dimension: Frontend performance and bundle weight (Next.js 16.2.10 App Router, Turbopack build)
verification_method: Ran `npm run build` from scratch against current main (HEAD 844e6c6, effectively identical working tree aside from an unrelated package.json/lockfile diff removing an unused 'workflow' dependency) and re-derived every number from the resulting .next output myself: text-extracted every prerendered .next/server/app/*.html, parsed .next/diagnostics/route-bundle-stats.json for firstLoadUncompressedJsBytes, re-brotli-compressed the cited chunks with Node zlib, scanned all 166 .next/static/chunks/*.js files for byte-size collisions and for recharts/toast/queryKey string fingerprints, and grepped source directly for every cited line/pattern. Results were reproduced identically across two independent from-scratch builds (BUILD_ID bpJTZmnBu5bJplT-L-Jse and a second run), so they are not build noise. The Supabase MCP tool required by the task brief (mcp__claude_ai_Supabase__execute_sql) was unavailable this session (not connected) — every claim resting on live production row counts (email_logs volumes, pg_stat_statements, live group/member/payment counts) could not be independently checked and is called out as unverified below rather than confirmed or refuted.
summary: 5 of 8 findings verified essentially as reported (1, 3, 4, 5, 8), with the byte-level numbers in 1 and 5 running consistently ~8-12% below what the finder reported (real, reproducible, just smaller) and finding 1 overcounting 'authenticated routes' by ~10. Finding 6 has a solid, confirmed core (the 1.43MB unoptimized master PNG, the exact code path) but its supporting 'next largest file is 88KB / 84% of public' claim is fabricated — the real public/ directory has five other images between 172KB and 395KB, and the logo is 48.5% of a 2.89MB directory, not 84% of 1.7MB. Findings 2 and 7 are REFUTED: two from-scratch production builds show zero duplicate-sized chunks anywhere in .next/static/chunks, and exactly ONE 358.3KB recharts vendor chunk exists, not six. The underlying source-level fact behind finding 2 (five route-local files import 'recharts' directly instead of through components/shared/charts.tsx) is real, but Turbopack already dedupes the actual library into a single shared chunk regardless of which file imports it, so the claimed 1.75-2.1MB bundle cost does not exist in the shipped output.

verified.title: All authenticated app-shell routes server-render an empty page shell (title only, or a bare loading/verifying string) — no real content
verified.evidence: I text-extracted every file under .next/server/app (strip <script>/<style>, strip tags, collapse entities) from a from-scratch build. Of 71 statically-prerendered pages inside the five client-shell route groups, ALL 71 render only a loading placeholder: 37 pages in (dashboard) and (member) — dashboard, loans, members, settings, contributions, accounting, analytics, billing, credit-scores, treasury, welfare, etc. — render exactly 39 visible characters (literally just the <title>, 'Kitabu Yetu — Build Vibrant Communities'); the 16 (admin) pages and 10 (enterprise) pages render 67 characters ('...Verifying backoffice/enterprise access...'); the 8 (reminder) pages render 62 characters ('...Loading Chama Reminder...'). All five route-group layouts open with 'use client' (app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:1, app/(admin)/layout.tsx:1, app/(member)/layout.tsx:1, app/(enterprise)/layout.tsx:1, app/(reminder)/layout.tsx:1), lib/api/client.ts:1 is 'use client' and reads the bearer token from localStorage on every call (confirmed at lib/api/client.ts:9-30, key 'ky_auth'), and app/status/page.tsx is verifiably the ONLY page in the app that both is an async server component and imports runtime code from lib/services — I checked all 7 other page.tsx files that reference '@/lib/services/*' and every one of them is a type-only `import type` inside a 'use client' file, which erases at compile time. Measured from .next/diagnostics/route-bundle-stats.json (own script, own brotli pass): the true count of routes under the five client-shell groups is 80 (not 90 — the extra 10 in the finder's count are the (auth) group's login/register/forgot-password pages, which use a SEPARATE, genuinely server-rendered layout and measurably do NOT have this problem: login.html carries 326 visible characters, admin-login.html 345, register.html 100). Average first-load JS across those 80 routes = 736.0 KB raw; the heaviest, /shares, = 815.2 KB raw / 216.5 KB brotli (not the claimed 782 KB average / 865 KB max — consistently ~6-8% lower in my build, but the same order of magnitude and the same conclusion).
verified.impact: Every one of these 80 routes ships no usable HTML — the browser must download and hydrate several hundred KB of JS before anything paints, then wait on API round-trips for content, exactly as claimed. This is the single largest, best-supported finding in the report and the numbers hold up under independent re-derivation, modulo the corrected route count and modestly smaller byte figures above. The PWA start_url ('/dashboard', confirmed in app/manifest.ts:8) does open directly onto one of these empty shells.
verified.recommendation: As the finder proposed: keep the client-side token model, but convert the static chrome (sidebars, headers, table scaffolding, empty states) in each of the five layouts into server components so the HTML is non-trivial, restricting 'use client' to the interactive leaves. This is a large, cross-cutting change, not a quick fix.
verified.note: Core claim fully reproduced. Corrections: true authenticated-route count is 80, not 90 (the (auth) group's 10 pages are server-rendered and do not belong in this bucket); the literal '39 characters' figure applies to 37 of the 71 pages — admin/enterprise pages show 67 chars and reminder pages show 62 chars, still an empty loading message, not real content, so the architectural conclusion still generalizes correctly even though the specific number doesn't. Byte figures (782KB avg / 865KB max) reproduce ~6-8% lower in my two from-scratch builds (736.0KB avg / 815.2KB max) — within normal build-to-build variance, not a material overstatement.

verified.title: recharts vendor code is NOT duplicated across chunks — Turbopack already collapses it into one shared 358.3KB chunk despite five files importing it directly
verified.evidence: Confirmed the source-level premise: app/(admin)/admin/analytics/_charts.tsx, app/(admin)/admin/billing-admin/_charts.tsx, app/(admin)/admin/_revenue-chart.tsx, app/(dashboard)/analytics/_charts.tsx and app/(dashboard)/credit-scores/[memberId]/_charts.tsx all `import ... from 'recharts'` directly rather than via components/shared/charts.tsx, and only admin/monitoring, admin/risk and design-system use the shared kit — exactly as claimed. But I could not reproduce the claimed duplication. I scanned all 166 files in .next/static/chunks from two independent from-scratch builds for byte-size collisions: BOTH builds have ZERO chunks sharing an identical size anywhere in the entire output (a script-level positive control confirms the detector works — an earlier, now-superseded build did surface one coincidental same-size pair unrelated to charts). Scanning specifically for recharts/ResponsiveContainer string fingerprints turns up exactly ONE 358.3KB chunk (0r43dqvfs5_qz.js, byte-identical across both from-scratch builds) containing the actual recharts library, plus small 1-49KB chunks that I mapped by exported component name (GrowthChart/TopGroupsChart -> 21.1KB, RevenueByPlanChart -> 1.1KB, ContributionsChart/RepaymentsChart/etc -> 19.2KB, ScoreHistoryChart -> 1.0KB, the shared TrendChart/BarSeriesChart/DonutChart/Sparkline kit -> 48.8KB) — these are just the app-level chart-configuration glue code for each route, not repeated copies of the ~360KB library. Git history explains why: commit 4fd4248 (Jul 20) deliberately introduced this exact per-route `next/dynamic(() => import('./_charts'))` pattern specifically to code-split recharts out of first-load JS (fixing a prior audit's Medium #26) — it was never routed through the shared kit, and Turbopack's own chunk-graph optimizer, not the shared-wrapper file, is what's deduplicating the actual library today.
verified.impact: None measurable. The claimed '1.75MB redundant JS' / 'zero cross-page cache reuse' does not exist in two from-scratch production builds — recharts genuinely ships once, in one chunk, referenced by every chart-bearing route.
verified.recommendation: The five files still deviate from the documented shared-kit convention in components/shared/charts.tsx, which is a legitimate (minor) code-consistency issue worth fixing opportunistically for maintainability and API uniformity — but not for the bundle-size reason claimed, since there is no bundle-size cost today.
verified.note: REFUTED on the central claim (six 358.3KB duplicate chunks / 2.1MB total). Reproduced zero duplicate chunks of any kind in two from-scratch builds. The finder's own evidence contained an internal red flag worth noting for calibration next time: they reported pairwise character-match ranging '4.5%-89.7%' between the supposed duplicates, which is far too low and inconsistent to be the same minified module with only renumbered IDs (that should read >95% identical) — a sign the six same-sized files they found were very likely a coincidental collision, not verified duplicate content.

verified.title: Dashboard blocks the entire page behind one boolean ORed across 11 independent queries — a known, previously-documented tradeoff, still real today
verified.evidence: Verified at current line numbers in app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx: 10 queries (useMembers, useContributions, useLoans, useWelfarePool, useWelfareRequests, plus useQuery calls for /mpesa/unrouted, /contributions/non-contributors, /accounting/reports?type=trial_balance, /analytics/executive?period=12mo, loansApi.upcomingRepayments) feed a `dashboardQueries` array at line 162; `const isDashboardLoading = dashboardQueries.some((q) => q.isLoading)` at line 174; and `if (isDashboardLoading)` returns a full-page Skeleton block at line 226. app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx:16 calls useEntitlements() (hooks/use-entitlements.ts:22, a real useQuery against billingApi.entitlements), independently confirming the 11th call. `grep -rn "\.some((q) => q\.isLoading)" app` returns exactly this one match, confirming the pattern is unique to this page as claimed. Notably, the surrounding code comment explicitly cites this as a deliberate decision from a prior document ('UX_UI_OPTIMIZATION_AUDIT_2026-08.md C5') made to replace an earlier, worse bug (confident-looking zeros shown during loading/failure) — this is a known, already-reasoned-about tradeoff being re-flagged, not a fresh discovery of an oversight.
verified.impact: As described: the slowest of 11 parallel requests gates the whole dashboard behind a full skeleton even when 10 have already returned, and because none of these fire until after the client-only shell (finding 1) hydrates, their latency stacks on top of, rather than overlaps with, the JS download. I could not verify the specific supporting numbers — 'pg_stat_statements shows none of these endpoints in the top 25 by mean execution time' and 'underlying data is tiny (9 groups, 37 members, 49 payments)' — because the Supabase MCP tool was unavailable this session (see note).
verified.recommendation: Render each stat card against its own query's loading state rather than gating the whole page on the slowest of 11; group only the tiles that genuinely need combined data. Separately reconsider whether /analytics/executive?period=12mo needs 12 months of buckets just to show three headline totals.
verified.note: Code mechanism and line numbers fully reproduced against current main. The DB-backed sub-claims (exact production row counts, pg_stat_statements ranking) are UNVERIFIED, not confirmed — the Supabase execute_sql tool specified in the task brief was not connected in this session (ToolSearch returned no match; a separate MCP_DOCKER server showed a connection failure, but the Supabase tool itself was simply absent from the available toolset). Treat those two specific sub-claims as not independently checked.

verified.title: Fraunces (117.9KB) is preload-hinted on every authenticated route despite zero usage there
verified.evidence: Reproduced with high precision from a from-scratch build. app/layout.tsx:11-16 loads Fraunces with axes ['opsz','SOFT'] and line ~101 applies `${inter.variable} ${fraunces.variable} ${dmMono.variable}` to <body> in the ROOT layout, so every route gets the hint. Measured the actual emitted font files by their content hash: b67966e0b83b2cd0 (Fraunces) = 120,724 bytes = 117.9KB; 83afe278b6a6bb3c (Inter) = 48,432B = 47.3KB; a73419dd2ba2d841 (DM Mono 500) = 8,724B = 8.5KB; 36363bfb06833f56 (DM Mono 400) = 8,688B = 8.5KB — total 186,568B = 182.2KB, matching the finder's figure almost to the byte. Verified all four appear as <link rel="preload" as="font"> on .next/server/app/dashboard.html, an authenticated route. Grepped 'font-display' (the only Tailwind path to var(--font-fraunces), confirmed at tailwind.config.ts:158) across the whole repo: 0 matches inside app/(dashboard), app/(admin), app/(member), app/(enterprise), or app/(reminder) — confirmed with five separate directory-scoped greps, all returning no files. The positive control holds too: font-mono (the legitimately-shared DM Mono utility) is used in 59 files, including many files inside the dashboard/admin route groups, so the check is genuinely distinguishing used from unused fonts rather than flagging everything.
verified.impact: As claimed: a first visit to any of the 80 authenticated routes fetches 117.9KB of a serif display font that route will never render, at preload priority, competing with the JS that already gates first paint (finding 1). One-time cost per cache lifetime, landing on the worst possible moment (cold first impression).
verified.recommendation: Move the Fraunces font variable off the root <body> onto a marketing-only wrapper (e.g. a class applied in components/marketing/page-shell.tsx or a marketing route-group layout) so Next only emits the preload hint on routes that use it.
verified.note: Byte-for-byte reproduction of the font-size and preload claims. Minor overstatement only in the supporting usage-count claims: font-display actually appears in 15-16 files (not 20; one of the 16 grep hits is the tailwind.config.ts definition itself and one is a code comment in app/layout.tsx, not real usage), and font-mono in 59 files (not 69) — neither affects the core conclusion.

verified.title: React Query / AuthProvider / Toaster runtime ships to all marketing and legal pages via the root layout
verified.evidence: app/layout.tsx wraps children in <Providers> (root layout, applies to all routes); providers/index.tsx:1 is 'use client' and instantiates QueryClientProvider, AuthProvider (lib/auth/context.tsx:1, 'use client'), and <Toaster />, exactly as claimed. I computed the intersection of firstLoadChunkPaths across every route in route-bundle-stats.json myself: 11 common chunks (not 13), 558.8KB raw / 147.0KB brotli baseline shared by literally every route (not 618KB/158KB — ~10% lower, same conclusion). Within that baseline I independently fingerprinted two chunks carrying the provider stack by grepping for 'toast' and 'queryKey' identifier counts: one at 34,057B (34.2KB, 33 toast + 13 queryKey matches) and one at 27,353B (26.7KB, 55 toast + 11 queryKey matches) — sizes match the finder's cited 34.2KB/26.7KB almost exactly. Brotli-compressed these two myself: 9,912B + 8,259B = 18,171B = 17.75KB, matching the claimed '~18KB brotli' precisely. Confirmed 24 of the 26 non-(auth) marketing/legal page.tsx files (design-system and unauthorized are the exceptions) are server components with no 'use client'.
verified.impact: As claimed: every anonymous marketing visitor downloads and boots an unused data-fetching client, auth context, and toast portal — about 18KB brotli of genuinely dead runtime on the pages most sensitive to load time. One correction: I checked the finder's specific example set (legal/privacy, legal/terms, legal/data-protection, pricing, products, support, and home) and found six of those seven (everything except home) DO measure an identical first-load JS size — 608,366B = 594.1KB raw (not 653KB, but genuinely identical across those six, so the 'shared baseline dominates their payload' point holds). The home page '/' is NOT identical to the other six as claimed — it measures 691,010B = 674.8KB raw with one extra chunk, ~80KB heavier, presumably from homepage-specific code.
verified.recommendation: Move <Providers> down into the group layouts that actually need it (dashboard/admin/member/enterprise/reminder/auth), leaving the root layout to only supply html/body/fonts/metadata. Pairs naturally with the Fraunces fix since both are root-layout scoping errors.
verified.note: Core mechanism and the two provider-chunk sizes reproduced with high precision (brotli total matches almost exactly). Two corrections: the shared baseline is 11 chunks/558.8KB/147.0KB brotli in my build, not 13/618KB/158KB (~10% lower, same conclusion); and the home page '/' does not share the identical 653KB (nor my measured 594.1KB) figure with the other six cited pages — it is measurably heavier and should not have been grouped with them as 'identical'.

verified.title: 1.43MB unoptimized master logo PNG is served raw (bypassing next/image) into outbound emails
verified.evidence: public/brand/kitabu-yetu-logo.png confirmed at exactly 1,468,964 bytes (1.43MB), and I parsed its IHDR chunk directly: 1024x1024, bit depth 8, color type 6 (RGBA) — exact match to the claim. Confirmed the code path exactly as cited: lib/brand.ts:46-48 getBrandLogoUrl() returns the raw `${base}/brand/kitabu-yetu-logo.png` path (no image optimizer involved); emails/components/layout.tsx:61 renders ``; lib/email/templates/engine.ts:91 sets `logoUrl = branding.logoUrl ?? getBrandLogoUrl()` and line 109 renders it at width=72/height=72 (not 36x36 — that 36x36 figure is only accurate for the emails/components/layout.tsx sender; the DB-driven template engine renders the same 1.43MB file at 72x72, still roughly 20,000x more pixels than needed rather than 40,000x). components/branding/BrandLogo.tsx:1,35 confirmed using next/image (the safe path) for on-site UI. scripts/generate-icons.ts:11 confirmed already using sharp to resize this exact source file, supporting the recommendation that the pipeline to fix this already exists. The supporting directory-size claim does NOT hold: I measured public/ at 3,027,692 bytes (2.89MB, not 1.7MB), the logo is 48.5% of it (not 84%), and the next-largest file is NOT 88KB — it's public/img/bookkeeper.jpg at 395,511 bytes (386KB), followed by hero-one.jpg (218KB), enterprise.jpg (190KB), and fundraise.jpg (172KB), all far larger than the claimed 88KB runner-up.
verified.impact: The core waste is real: recipients whose email clients load images download a 1.43MB file to paint a 36px or 72px logo. I could not verify the live email_logs volume claim (524 sent / 43,081 failed / 3,887 queued) — the Supabase tool was unavailable this session — so I cannot confirm today's actual blast radius or the '10,000 delivered emails -> ~14GB egress' projection, though the arithmetic is directionally sound if the volume figures are accurate.
verified.recommendation: As the finder proposed: generate a small dedicated email raster (72x72 or so) with the existing sharp-based scripts/generate-icons.ts pipeline and point getBrandLogoUrl() at it instead of the 1024x1024 master.
verified.note: The asset itself, its dimensions, and every code-path citation are confirmed exactly. Two things in the surrounding evidence are wrong and should not be repeated: the 'next largest file is 88KB / 84% of a 1.7MB public/ dir' claim is fabricated (actual: 2.89MB dir, 48.5%, next-largest is 386KB) and the title's '36x36' figure applies to only one of the two cited senders (the other renders at 72x72). The live email-volume numbers are unverified, not confirmed, due to a tooling gap this session.

verified.title: No further chunk duplication exists beyond the (already-refuted) recharts claim
verified.evidence: I scanned every file in .next/static/chunks (166 files) for exact byte-size collisions across two independent from-scratch production builds. Both builds: ZERO chunks anywhere share an identical size — no 35.0KB pair, no 32.1KB pair, no 23.0KB pair, no 17.4KB pair, and no pair at any other size. My detector is validated as functional: run against an earlier (now-superseded, pre-rebuild) .next output, it did surface one coincidental same-size pair (25.4KB, unrelated to any of the four claimed pairs), so the method is capable of finding real collisions when they exist — it simply finds none in the current, correctly-built output.
verified.impact: None. The claimed ~107KB of redundant CDN bytes and cross-route cache-miss cost does not exist in the shipped bundle.
verified.recommendation: No action needed; nothing to fix here.
verified.note: REFUTED. Given this finding already carried low confidence and explicitly built on the same (now-refuted) methodology as finding 2, and produces zero matches in two from-scratch builds, I have no basis to confirm any of the four specific pairs cited.

verified.title: Full installable PWA manifest with no service worker — offline/flaky-network opens to a dead shell
verified.evidence: app/manifest.ts confirmed: start_url '/dashboard', display 'standalone', a shortcuts array with entries named 'Dashboard' and 'Contributions' (lines 71-81). app/layout.tsx confirmed setting appleWebApp.capable:true and a startupImage array (lines 55-59+). Grepped app, components, lib, providers and package.json for serviceWorker / navigator.serviceWorker / workbox / next-pwa: zero matches anywhere. Confirmed no public/sw.js or public/service-worker.js exists. Confirmed scripts/generate-icons.ts already imports and uses `sharp` (supports the recommendation that icon tooling exists to build on). Combined with finding 1 (confirmed above), the installable app's start_url genuinely renders an empty 39-character shell with no service worker to fall back on.
verified.impact: As claimed: an installed PWA opened without connectivity has no cached shell and no cached data, so it cannot degrade gracefully — it just spins. This is entirely dependent on finding 1 being true, which it is.
verified.recommendation: As the finder proposed: don't build this before finding 1's server-rendering work lands — a service worker caching an empty shell buys nothing. Sequence it as a follow-on.
